analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | Europe reads | 3 pts from EPS | WHR JBLU GBX CLW 27 Oct 2026
key_insights: Desk morning color: US S&P futures flat after yesterday's gains. Markets are digesting capital raises across technology. KOSPI is up 309bps and Japan up 173bps, while Europe trades lower with France off 24bps as regional consumer confidence hits 13 year lows.

Commodities and rates: WTI at $102 and Brent at $116, both at local highs. Gold is below $4k and silver is down double digits over the last week. The 10-year yield is 4.98% and Bitcoin is below $80k. A Fed hold is expected in a big central bank week.

Europe earnings reads: WRT1V -10% on an order miss after a debated upgrade, with Energy driving the order beat and Marine missing. ASSAB flat on a Q3 EBIT beat, with margins 40bps ahead on the Americas. ALFA +1% on a 14% Q3 order beat and good margin execution despite a sales miss. P911 +2% on a profit beat despite lower volumes.

Desk view on risk: front-end rates have stabilized, which is good for risk. High energy prices more likely produce chop than a sustained selloff absent escalation. Credit is the main worry, still flashing yellow to red relative to equities. A calmer credit market could be a catalyst for a broader rally.

Hyperscalers and the Fed are the main events this week. The desk's four focus points are capex (flat or up is fine, down would be bad for suppliers), backlog conversion into revenue, free cash flow conversion in out quarters, and financing mix (equity versus debt).
Flows: after weeks of net selling of tech, clients began buying on the other side yesterday, at least in Europe. The desk's modal view is that markets chop until next week's political events clear.

Earnings point 1: defense is catching a bid, which the desk does not attribute to defensive rotation or positioning. LMT (consensus long) and NOC (consensus short) are up similar mid single digits on clean results. The desk cites prior underperformance, progress on agreements that could lift volumes, and the midterms as a favorable backdrop into year end. GD and LHX report this week, and LHX expectations are particularly low.

Earnings point 2: non-residential construction stands out favorably. Warehouse, retail and commercial office are getting better or less worse, and URI commentary, ALLE organic growth and FAST are all supportive. The desk thinks this could set up CAT tactically this week after a large sell off. Seasonality favors residential names into November, and ALLE is now the top member of the homebuilding index.

Earnings point 3: the desk thinks the Europe-read moves have already happened and suggests the other side may make more sense for US prints. Pairs named are ATCOA to IR, ELUXB to WHR and SCHN to OTIS.

CLW Q3 missed slightly on sales and EBITDA. Management expects a continued recovery in SBS conditions despite transportation and chemical cost headwinds, and cites RISI forecasting improved pricing later this quarter and into next year.
GBX Q4 missed on EPS and revenue. 2027 revenue guidance is above consensus at $2.8-3.2bn, but the EBIT margin guide of 7-7.5% is well below the 10% consensus.
JBLU Q3 loss was wider than consensus on roughly in-line revenue. Q4 guidance: RASM +18-22%, ASM +3-4%, flat CASMx, capex $300mm.

WHR Q3 was a large miss. It reported a loss against an expected profit, ongoing EBIT well below consensus, and sales below consensus. Full year revenue outlook was cut to $14.5bn from $15bn, and the EPS outlook moved from a positive $2.5-3.00 to a loss of $1.30.
Implied earnings moves flagged by the desk: WHR 10% (call at 8am), JBLU 15% (call at 10am), CLW 7% and GBX 9% (calls at 5pm).

Calendar this week: ADP, durable orders and consumer confidence today, FOMC Wednesday, claims and PCE Thursday, Eurozone CPI and Chicago PMI Friday. Large US industrial and materials reporters include BA, UPS, PCAR, GEV, CARR, HWM and GD.

earnings_insights: CLW reported Q3 sales of $385mm vs $392mm consensus and EBITDA of $24mm vs $25mm consensus (reported 10/26 post-market). Call at 5pm with a 7% implied move. Management expects continued SBS recovery and cites RISI forecasting improved pricing later this quarter and into next year.

GBX reported Q4 EPS of $0.39 vs $0.80 consensus on revenue of $591mm vs $605mm consensus (reported 10/26 post-market). Guided 2027 revenue of $2.8-3.2bn vs $2.7bn consensus and EBIT margin of 7-7.5% vs 10% consensus. Call at 5pm with a 9% implied move.

JBLU reported a Q3 loss of 60c vs a 55c loss consensus on revenue of about $2.8bn, roughly in line (reported 10/27 pre-market). Guides Q4 RASM +18-22%, ASM +3-4%, flat CASMx and capex of $300mm. Call at 10am with a 15% implied move.

WHR reported a Q3 loss of $0.21 vs a $0.76 positive consensus, ongoing EBIT well below $97mm vs $176mm consensus, and sales of $3.68bn vs $3.91bn consensus (reported 10/26 post-market). Full year revenue outlook cut to $14.5bn from $15bn. Ongoing loss per share guide of $1.30 vs prior positive EPS of $2.5-3.00. Call at 8am with a 10% implied move.

European Q3 reads: WRT1V orders missed with Energy ahead and Marine behind, sales in line, EBIT modestly ahead, guidance unchanged. ASSAB EBIT beat on in-line sales with margins 40bps ahead. ALFA orders beat by 14% with a sales miss, driven by Ocean. P911 profit beat on lower volumes.
US earnings so far: LMT and NOC reported clean results and both rose mid single digits. ALLE organic growth, URI commentary and FAST were described as supportive for non-residential construction.
Upcoming reports flagged by the desk: GD and LHX this week, and CAT tactically. Further names report Tuesday through Friday, including BA, UPS, PCAR, GEV, CARR, HWM and GD (Friday).
